notes:
PlaybackStore rearchitecture COMPLETE — phase E retired playingUntil, the last side-channel, closing work that ran A through E across four sessions. One source of truth for what a zone is playing. Phase C stays closed as a negative result. Also shipped: Xcode synchronized folders (no more hand-editing the project file for new sources) and two transport-optimism bugs, one of which made local playback's grace window depend on queue length.

THE SIMULATOR TEST HARNESS is the session's real output, and it closes the asymmetry that slowed every playback investigation this week: the speakers were fully visible over SOAP and the app was not, so 'the app shows X but the speaker is doing Y' always needed Tom to look at his phone. tools/sonos.py drives and queries the speakers, with a testing() context that enforces the nominated zone list, mutes, and restores prior state even if the body throws. tools/sim.py finds the app container by metadata rather than a remembered UUID, reads the database READ-ONLY so a running app cannot be corrupted, and snapshots the device keychain as well as the container — the keychain is device-level, so a container-only copy silently loses the NAS credentials. Guardrails live in tools/test-zones.json, enforced in code rather than remembered.

IT FOUND A BUG IMMEDIATELY, AND THE FIX FAILED INSTRUCTIVELY. Adding a share queues a scan and raises a confirmation alert that dies untouched under a second, so a new share is never scanned. The detail view is created twice 43ms apart during the add navigation and the alert was bound to @State on it. Rebinding to the coordinator did not help: SwiftUI writes FALSE BACK into whatever an alert is bound to when the host view churns, so the setter read that as a dismissal and cleared the queued scan. Reverted rather than iterated on — because the better answer is not to have the dialog.

WHICH IS THE ACTUAL OUTCOME. Tom stepped back from the bug to the process: nobody adds a share and then does not want its music, so the dialog asks a question with one sensible answer. Roon calls this Storage and never makes you start a scan of a source you just added. Logged as fAutoScanOnShareAdd and deferred, since the warning it replaces needs a progress view that does not exist yet. fSourceAvailability came out of the same thread, carrying the catch that would otherwise be rediscovered: the phone is not in the audio path, so deriving availability from what the phone can reach would grey out the whole local library every time the user leaves the house.

ALSO: Diagnostics screen in Settings now holds the debug log and the SMB probes, which had been cluttering the share menu. Landing it exposed a pre-existing layout bug where the floating tab bar overlays the scroll view without taking layout space, leaving the last Settings row visible but untappable; padding raised as an interim measure pending the redesign.

VELOCITY ACCOUNTING now captures testing that is not attached to a shipping feature — a regression pass or a session spent validating a suite previously consumed owner hours and earned nothing. test_hrs and test_equiv_hrs added to the session record with an explicit three-way split so building a suite (a normal feature size) is never double-counted against validating or running it.
